subject: capybara
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: capybara with a small bird on its head.
Style: whimsical.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a skeleton plan for the capybara model—hips, spine, neck, head, and four legs with simple IK—sized at roughly 1.1m long and 0.5m tall, facing forward, before writing the actual rigging code.

I'll simplify neck to two joints (neck1, neck2), then attach the head joint to the last neck joint with its own position and direction. For the head shape, I'll use a frustum box extending from the skull to a blunt muzzle, sizing width and height at each end, then add a darker muzzle and nose box at the front.

Now I'm placing the jaw under the head as a smaller frustum box, dark spherical eyes positioned using head-local forward/up/left coordinates (mirrored for left and right sides), plus small rounded ears on top-back and nostril details. I'm also figuring out where the head sits relative to the neck's end position so a bird can perch on top, and now I'm moving on to building the four short legs using a limb function with lengths and bend parameters.

Working out leg geometry and sweep radii...

I'm sketching a whimsical touch too: a small bird perched near the head, built from basic shapes like spheres for body/head, a cone beak, flattened wing shapes, and a slab tail, all around 0.1m scale with a pale blue tufted look. I'm also considering whether to add eye details via textured planes or just keep things simple with spheres.

Figuring out eye placement...

Now I'm planning the fur color palette: browns for the main coat, darker brown for shading, tan for the belly, and a dark nose, then moving into writing the actual head geometry code with the frustum box shape and bone positioning.

Adding muzzle and jaw geometry...

Working out bird placement...

Still positioning body parts...
